vampireDrain.body: Idle energy lost while the car is parked and not charging. We compute it as the % of battery used per hour while the vehicle reports gear=Park and is not in motion.
vampireDrain.avgRate: Mean battery loss per hour while parked and not charging across the selected period.
vampireDrain.totalLoss: Estimated kWh lost to vampire drain across all parked sessions in the selected period.
vampireDrain.worstSession: Single parked session with the largest % battery drop.
vampireDrain.score: 0–100 health score derived from your drain rate vs. fleet expectations. Higher is better.

sleepEfficiency.body: Share of parked time the car spent in true low-power sleep (vs. idle/online). Higher is better — more sleep means less vampire drain and lower battery wear.
sleepEfficiency.timeToSleep: Average minutes from when the car parks to when it enters low-power sleep.
sleepEfficiency.sentryDrain: Battery loss per hour while Sentry Mode is active. Sentry keeps cameras and computers on, which adds noticeable drain.
sleepEfficiency.sentryCost: Estimated monthly electricity cost of Sentry-related drain, using your configured per-kWh rate.

driveScore.body: 0–100 score derived from smoothness of acceleration, braking, and cornering combined with energy efficiency. Tunable in Settings → Driving.

regenEfficiency.body: Energy recovered through regenerative braking divided by total energy used during driving. Higher is better — Tesla cars typically reach 15–30% recovery in mixed driving.

fleetTelemetryHealthy.body: Last MQTT message received within the last 5 minutes. Stale means no recent message; check the fleet-telemetry deployment.

cooldownMin.body: Minimum minutes between consecutive alerts from this rule, regardless of how often the underlying signal crosses the threshold.

signal.layers: TeslaSync exposes three live-state layers: L1 — in-process signal store on the API pod that ingested the telemetry (lowest latency, scope-limited to that pod). L2 — Redis-backed shared cache of latest values, visible to every pod, used for cross-pod live reads and SSE fanout. log — TimescaleDB signal_log history, authoritative for analytics, charts, and point-in-time reconstruction.
signal.live: Live mode streams real-time signal values via Server-Sent Events (SSE). The chart maintains a rolling 5-minute window throttled to 2 Hz updates.
signal.stale: A signal is marked stale when its last-seen value in Redis is older than 2 minutes — treat with caution; the vehicle may be offline or the pipeline may be backed up.
signal.snapshot: A snapshot is a point-in-time view of every signal value at a single timestamp. The diff falls back to signal_log within the last 30 days when the live layer doesn't have it.
signal.diff: Server-side comparison between two snapshots. Unchanged signals are omitted from the result to reduce noise.
signal.sourceLayer: The layer that supplied this value: L1 (in-process), L2 (Redis), LOG (TimescaleDB history), or STALE (older than 2 minutes).
signal.deltaCol: Numeric difference (and percent change) between Window A and Window B for this signal. 'changed' is shown for non-numeric values that differ.

fsm.type: Finite-state machine. Tracks vehicle high-level state (driving, charging, parked, online, asleep, offline) and the transitions between them. Sub-FSMs cover drive, charge, command, and notification lifecycles.
fsm.liveState: The current state the FSM resolved to from the most recent telemetry. The FSM stays in a terminal state until external evidence (telemetry or poll) triggers an explicit transition out.

replay.power: Instantaneous battery power at this point on the trip. Negative values indicate regenerative braking (energy flowing back into the pack); positive values indicate motor draw.
replay.battery: State-of-charge percentage at this point. Drops indicate energy use; rises indicate regen or DC-fast-charging during a drive.
replay.range: Estimated rated range remaining at this position based on EPA rated efficiency. Differs from real-world range, which depends on speed, terrain, climate, and load.

battery.soh: State of Health — current usable capacity divided by the original rated capacity, expressed as a percentage. Higher is better; new packs start at 100%.
battery.capacity: Estimated current usable energy capacity of the pack in kWh, derived from the SoH and the original rated capacity.
battery.degradationRate: Annualised rate of capacity loss based on observed SoH trend. Combines calendar fade (time at temperature/SoC) and cycle fade (kWh throughput).
battery.totalCycles: Cumulative full-pack equivalent cycles. One cycle = one full discharge + one full charge worth of energy (partial cycles add up over time).
battery.avgDoD: Average Depth of Discharge per cycle — how deeply the pack is typically discharged before being recharged. Shallower cycles cause less wear.

lifetime.avgEfficiency: Average energy used per unit distance across the whole driving history (Wh/km). Lower is better — temperature, speed, and terrain are the main drivers.

charging.peakPower: Maximum charging power observed during this session, in kW. DC fast-charging tapers above ~80% SoC; AC charging stays roughly flat.
charging.avgPower: Time-averaged charging power across the session. Always lower than peak when the session includes a taper or initial ramp.
charging.socRange: The starting and ending state-of-charge percentages for this session. Wider ranges generally mean longer sessions and more taper.
charging.chargeCurve: Power vs SoC curve for the session. Tapering — the gradual drop in power as the battery approaches full — is inherent to lithium chemistry and is not a fault. Sudden drops below the curve indicate derating: the charger or battery is throttling power because of cell or ambient temperature limits.
charging.kwhPerHour: Average kWh added per hour across the session. Useful for estimating how long a future session will take at the same charger.

settings.region: Tesla account region (NA, EU, CN). Determines which Fleet API endpoint TeslaSync calls. Refresh after changing your Tesla account country.
settings.gasPriceAutoPoll: When enabled, TeslaSync automatically fetches U.S. average gasoline prices from the EIA. Used to compute fuel-savings vs. driving an EV.
settings.gasPricePollInterval: How often the gas-price worker polls the EIA. Daily catches price spikes; weekly is plenty for most users and is gentler on the upstream feed.
settings.notificationChannels: Where alert messages are delivered. Add channels (Discord, Slack, email, webhook, ntfy, Pushover, Telegram) before alerts can fire.
settings.appearanceDensity: Controls row height, padding, and font sizes across tables and dashboards. Compact fits more on screen; comfortable is easier to read on large displays.
settings.chartPalette: Colour scheme used for chart series. Vivid is the default high-contrast palette; muted reduces visual noise; print is grayscale-friendly for exports.
settings.timeFormat: 12-hour (1:30 PM) vs 24-hour (13:30) display across timestamps. Affects all surfaces — drives, charging, alerts, telemetry charts.
settings.uiTheme: Light / dark / system theme. System follows your OS preference and switches automatically when your OS toggles between modes.
settings.language: Display language for UI strings. TeslaSync ships English; community translations may be incomplete for newer features.
settings.weekStart: First day of the week in calendar pickers and weekly aggregations. ISO 8601 default is Monday; many U.S. users prefer Sunday.
settings.electricityCost: Cost per kWh used to compute charging spend across drives, charging sessions, and TCO analytics. Currency follows the Currency setting above.

alertStudio.cooldown: Minimum minutes between repeat firings of this rule. Prevents the same condition from spamming your channels (e.g. battery at 19% triggering once per minute).
alertStudio.severity: Visual / routing priority — info, warn, or critical. Channels can subscribe to specific severities to keep critical alerts from being drowned out by chatty info ones.
alertStudio.alertBehavior: Pick 'Notify on event' for one-time confirmations like 'vehicle locked' or 'charging done'. Pick 'Re-alert until resolved' for ongoing safety concerns like 'vehicle unlocked' or 'door open'.
alertStudio.kind: Signal threshold compares a single live telemetry value (e.g. BatteryLevel < 20). Computed metric aggregates over a time window (e.g. cost > $5 in last 24h).
alertStudio.vehicleId: Restricts the rule to a single vehicle. Leave blank to apply across every vehicle on the account.
alertStudio.operator: Comparison applied to the signal value: =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, between, any change. Some operators only apply to numeric signals.
alertStudio.testMessage: Message body sent when the rule fires. Use {{SignalName}} placeholders to interpolate the current value into the notification.

automations.triggerType: What kicks the automation off — a time schedule, a signal threshold crossing, a geofence enter/exit, or another automation completing.
automations.operator: How the trigger or condition value is compared (=, !=, <, >, between, etc.). Numeric operators are only available for numeric signals.
automations.conditionLogic: When multiple conditions are configured, ALL must pass (AND) or ANY must pass (OR) for the actions to run.
automations.debounce: Minimum milliseconds between consecutive runs of this automation. Protects against duplicate triggers when a signal flickers across the threshold.
automations.geofence: A named circular region defined in /locations. Automations can react when the vehicle enters or exits the region.
automations.timeWindow: Time-of-day range (e.g. 22:00–06:00) and timezone. The condition only passes during that window in the chosen timezone.
automations.otherAutomation: Make this automation depend on another automation's recent state — e.g. only run if 'Morning prep' has not run today.
automations.signal: The vehicle telemetry signal this condition reads. Booleans use true/false, 'state' uses keywords like online/asleep, all others compare numeric values.
automations.cronExpr: Standard 5-field cron syntax (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Use the simple mode above for the most common schedules.
automations.timezone: IANA time zone used to interpret the start/end window. Defaults to your browser zone if left blank.
automations.dwellMinutes: How many minutes the vehicle must stay inside the geofence before this dwell trigger fires.

channels.webhookUrl: Full HTTPS URL TeslaSync POSTs the JSON body to. Discord and Slack provide their own webhook endpoints; for custom services use the generic Webhook channel.
channels.hmacSecret: Optional shared secret. When set, TeslaSync signs every request with HMAC-SHA256 in the X-TeslaSync-Signature header so receivers can verify authenticity.
channels.headersJson: Extra HTTP headers as a JSON object — e.g. {"Authorization": "Bearer XYZ"}. Useful for receivers that require API keys outside the URL.
channels.bodyTemplate: Optional JSON template for the request body. Use {{message}}, {{severity}}, {{timestamp}} placeholders. If omitted, TeslaSync sends its default JSON envelope.
channels.smtpHost: Mail server hostname (e.g. smtp.gmail.com). Most providers use port 587 with STARTTLS; check your provider's docs for the right host + port pair.
channels.smtpPort: SMTP server port. 587 for STARTTLS (recommended), 465 for implicit TLS, 25 for plain (insecure — only on local relays).
channels.smtpPassword: SMTP password or app-specific password. Stored encrypted at rest. Many providers (Gmail, Microsoft 365) require an app password rather than your account password.
channels.botToken: Telegram BotFather token in the format `<id>:<secret>`. Create a bot via @BotFather on Telegram, then start a chat with it before TeslaSync can deliver.
channels.chatId: Numeric Telegram chat ID. For a private bot chat this is your user ID; for a group it's negative (e.g. -1001234567890).
channels.ntfyServer: Base URL of the ntfy server (e.g. https://ntfy.sh for the public server, or your self-hosted instance).
channels.ntfyTopic: Topic name on the ntfy server. Anyone with the topic name can subscribe — pick something hard to guess for sensitive alerts.
channels.method: HTTP method TeslaSync uses for outbound delivery. POST is universal; some receivers require PUT or PATCH.
channels.nameLabel: Friendly identifier shown in the channel list and on alert delivery logs. Has no functional impact — pick anything memorable.
channels.configSection: Provider-specific credentials and routing details. Required fields vary by channel type. All secrets are encrypted at rest.
channels.testHint: Use the "Send Test" button after saving to verify your configuration. Tests bypass severity filters but otherwise match real delivery.

settings.title: Helix
settings.subtitle: Optional. Helix is off by default; nothing is enabled until you opt in here.
settings.bannerOff: Helix is off. Your app works fully without it. Enable a mode above to opt in.

mode.offHint: Helix is off. The app works fully without it.
mode.localHint: Use a private model on your network (e.g. Ollama). No data leaves your install.
mode.cloudHint: Use a cloud provider (e.g. OpenAI). Requires an API key.

provider.label: Provider configuration
provider.baseUrlHint: Must resolve to a private network address (loopback, RFC1918, link-local, or ULA).
provider.apiKeyHint: Stored encrypted. Never displayed once saved.
provider.costCapHint: Daily cap on cloud spending. 0 disables the cap.
provider.localExplainer: Local-only mode never sends data outside your network. The validator pins the resolved IP at save time to defend against later DNS rebinding.
provider.validateOptional: Validation is optional but recommended — it catches mis-typed URLs and confirms the model is reachable.

provider.azureApiVersionHint: Leave blank to use the adapter default.
provider.azureDeploymentHint: Leave blank to reuse the Model field.

ai-provider-health.label: Helix provider health (ops)
ai-provider-health.description: Diagnostic endpoint that reports the active Helix provider and its capabilities. Off by default; enable only for ops debugging.

chatbot-llm.label: LLM chatbot
chatbot-llm.description: Conversational fleet assistant powered by an LLM. Falls back to the heuristic chatbot when Helix is off.

digest-narration.label: Weekly digest narration
digest-narration.description: Opt-in LLM narration of the weekly digest. The deterministic template digest remains the baseline when Helix is off.

yir-narration.label: Year-in-review narration
yir-narration.description: Opt-in LLM narration of the annual year-in-review slides. The deterministic template slides remain the baseline when Helix is off.

anomaly-explanations.label: Anomaly explanation narration
anomaly-explanations.description: Opt-in LLM narration that explains already-detected anomalies in plain language. The deterministic detector and safe-range explanations remain the baseline when Helix is off.

nl-alert-builder.label: Natural-language alert builder
nl-alert-builder.description: Opt-in LLM that drafts alert rules from a plain-language description. Drafts are typed AlertRule proposals that you review and save through the standard form; the manual AlertStudio remains the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

nl-automation-builder.label: Natural-language automation builder
nl-automation-builder.description: Opt-in LLM that drafts automation graphs (trigger, conditions, actions) from a plain-language description. Drafts are typed proposals that you review and save through the standard builder; the manual AutomationBuilder remains the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

nl-search.label: Natural-language search
nl-search.description: Opt-in LLM that searches your drives, charging sessions, and alerts from a plain-language description and narrates the matches. The typed search filters at /search remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

drive-coaching.label: Per-drive coaching
drive-coaching.description: Opt-in LLM that narrates an individual drive in 2-4 short paragraphs covering efficiency, regen use, and notable braking or acceleration moments. The deterministic per-drive stat cards, hero gauges, and energy summary remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

charging-diagnosis.label: Per-charging-session diagnosis
charging-diagnosis.description: Opt-in LLM that explains why a charging session was flagged trickle, expensive, low-power, or interrupted in 2-4 short paragraphs. The deterministic flag badges, hero gauges, and charge curve remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

rag-help.label: RAG-backed app help
rag-help.description: Opt-in LLM that answers natural-language questions about the application using its own documentation, runbooks, and i18n strings — with explicit citations to each source. The deterministic curated /help page links and tooltips remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

nl-drive-search-replay.label: Natural-language drive search and replay
nl-drive-search-replay.description: Opt-in LLM that finds a drive from a plain-language description and links straight to its replay. The typed search, filter chips, range picker, and vehicle selector on the Drives page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

speed-profile-insights.label: Speed-profile insights
speed-profile-insights.description: Opt-in LLM that interprets a drive's speed regime distribution — city / suburban / highway buckets, outliers, and a high-level route context envelope — in a few short sentences. The deterministic SpeedHistogramChart and summary metrics on the drive detail page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

route-efficiency-suggestions.label: Route-efficiency suggestions
route-efficiency-suggestions.description: Opt-in LLM that suggests lower-consumption habits and route choices grounded in your own route history — dominant route, kWh/100mi figure, and one or two concrete, non-mutating ideas to try yourself. The deterministic route comparison cards and kWh/100mi metrics on the Route Efficiency page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

trip-planner-llm-agent.label: Trip-planner LLM agent
trip-planner-llm-agent.description: Opt-in LLM agent that drafts a trip plan grounded in your own charging history along the corridor — origin and destination, current state of charge, minimum arrival state of charge, and one or two suggested stops drawn from places you have already charged at. The deterministic heuristic trip planner, manual form, map, and Plan button on the Trip Planner page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

smart-charge-schedule-suggestion.label: Smart-charge schedule suggestion
smart-charge-schedule-suggestion.description: Opt-in LLM agent that proposes a time-of-use-optimized charge schedule by delegating to the canonical charge-planner optimizer — target state of charge, departure time, rate plan, and a one or two sentence narration of the proposed window. The manual schedule form, deterministic optimizer, rate timeline, and Schedule button on the Smart Charge page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

battery-health-forecast-narrative.label: Battery health forecast narrative
battery-health-forecast-narrative.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that explains the deterministic battery-health forecast — current state of health, projected degradation slope, dominant charging-habit drivers, and the top one or two risk factors — grounded in the same numeric envelope the chart renders. The deterministic Capacity Trend & Prediction chart, hero metric cards, insights, and recommendations on the Battery Health page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

charging-curve-fingerprint-clustering.label: Charging-curve fingerprint clustering
charging-curve-fingerprint-clustering.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that names and explains each deterministic charging-curve cluster fingerprint — peak power tier (L1 / L2 / DC fast), session count per cluster, ramp shape, dominant charger type, and total energy per session — grounded in the same per-cluster envelope the curves render. The deterministic charging-curve charts, per-session labels, and distribution panel on the Charging Curve page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

cost-forecast-narration.label: Cost forecast narration
cost-forecast-narration.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that explains the deterministic charging-cost forecast — historical monthly trend, projected cost / cost_low / cost_high band, home-vs-supercharger split, and the top deterministic insight — grounded in the same numeric envelope the chart renders, and honest that the band is an APPROXIMATE prediction interval rather than a strict 95% confidence interval. The deterministic cost forecast chart, summary cards, breakdown, savings calculator, monthly cost table, time-of-use analysis, lifetime summary, and environmental impact card on the Cost Analysis page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

period-compare-narration.label: Period compare narration
period-compare-narration.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that explains the deterministic period-over-period analytics on the Period Compare page — which one or two metrics moved most between Period A and Period B, with directional phrasing keyed to the percent_change sign, and explicit honesty about zero-baseline windows and best-effort cost figures. The deterministic Period A vs Period B metric cards, side-by-side bar chart, comparison table, and insights panel remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

lifetime-stats-qa.label: Lifetime stats Q&A
lifetime-stats-qa.description: Opt-in LLM Q&A surface that answers natural-language questions about your all-time stats — total drives, total distance, charging savings, achievements, personal records, ownership timeline — by routing through two read-only tools that quote the same deterministic envelope the Lifetime Stats dashboard renders. The narrator never invents numbers and is honest about zero-data vehicles. The deterministic Lifetime Stats hero card, key-stats grid, achievements gallery, fun-facts cards, personal-records panel, and ownership timeline remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

incident-timeline-summarizer.label: Incident timeline summarizer
incident-timeline-summarizer.description: Opt-in LLM summarizer that condenses one incident's chronological timeline into a 3-6 sentence factual summary — what happened, what investigation steps the operator took, and how it resolved — by routing through two read-only tools that quote the same deterministic envelope the canonical incident page renders. The narrator never invents updates and never speculates about root cause. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-incident tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via operator-authored text. The deterministic incident timeline list, append-update form, and lifecycle controls on the per-incident page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

data-repair-suggestions.label: Data repair suggestions
data-repair-suggestions.description: Opt-in LLM that proposes a typed repair plan (close, discard, or partial-update) for one stale charging session or drive from the inventory shown on the Data Repair page. PROPOSE-ONLY: the LLM routes through two propose-only tools that share the same per-kind update_fields allowlist used by the canonical handler, and the user reviews the typed proposal in the Helix panel and clicks the canonical Save / Close / Discard button on the baseline form to apply it. The LLM never writes. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-row mutation proposal to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via operator-authored start_place / end_place fields. The deterministic stale-session list and per-row repair forms on the Data Repair page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

signal-explorer-nl-filter.label: Signal explorer NL filter
signal-explorer-nl-filter.description: Opt-in LLM that translates a natural-language filter request (e.g. "battery level for yesterday") into a typed SignalFilter draft the Signal Explorer page can apply with one click. PROPOSE-ONLY: the LLM routes through two propose-only tools that enforce the same per-vehicle signal catalog and range/per-page enumerations the deterministic SignalSelector + RangePicker + PER_PAGE Select honour, and the user reviews the typed proposal in the Helix panel and clicks Apply to copy it into the form. The LLM never edits filter state directly. Per-request scope binding rejects any signal name not in the in-scope per-vehicle catalog and any vehicle_id mismatch to defend against prompt-injection. The deterministic SignalSelector, RangePicker, page-size Select, and Explore / Live buttons on /signals/explorer remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

vampire-drain-explanation.label: Vampire-drain explanation
vampire-drain-explanation.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that explains the deterministic vampire-drain (idle energy loss) signal — recent average / median / p95 idle drain rate per day, the worst recent idle window (start, duration, drain %, ambient temperature), and the per-event driver (Sentry on, climate on, very long parked window) most strongly correlated with elevated drain — grounded in the same numeric envelope the cards render, and honest that the per-event driver attribution is correlational rather than causal. The deterministic vampire-drain stats, per-event timeline, and typical-vs-worst cards on the Vampire Drain page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

preheat-precool-recommender.label: Preheat and precool recommender
preheat-precool-recommender.description: Opt-in LLM agent that proposes a preheat or precool window — start time, end time, target cabin temperature, mode (preheat | precool) — by combining your typical departure timestamp with the vehicle's current cabin and outside temperatures. The proposal is structured and propose-only: review the typed draft in the Helix panel and click Apply on the existing climate-controls UI to save it; Helix never creates a schedule directly. The deterministic Climate Control page (HVAC banner, status cards, efficiency panel, history table, seat-heater controls, manual departure-time heuristic) remains the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

cabin-temperature-impact-narrative.label: Cabin temperature impact narrative
cabin-temperature-impact-narrative.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that explains how outside ambient temperature affects this vehicle's driving efficiency — which temperature bucket runs most efficiently, the relative consumption gap between the best and worst bucket, and the 12-month seasonal trend (cold-weather dip vs mild-weather recovery) — grounded strictly in the same bucketed-efficiency aggregates and monthly seasonal trend the chart renders, and honest that the surface is a descriptive aggregate of recent drives rather than a forecast or regression model. The deterministic Temperature Impact page (bucketed-efficiency chart, monthly seasonal trend, summary metric cards, recent drives table) remains the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

tire-pressure-trend-reasoning.label: Tire-pressure trend reasoning
tire-pressure-trend-reasoning.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that explains the recent 30-day trend in this vehicle's four corner tire pressures — which tires are trending up, down, or stable, the most likely deterministic driver of any deviation (cold-weather correlation when all four corners trend together with a parallel ambient-temperature drop, single-corner slow-leak signature when one corner's rate is materially worse), and any actionable threshold crossing — grounded strictly in the same TpmsPressure* and OutsideTemp signal-log change feed the gauges render, and honest that the per-corner slope is a descriptive linear extrapolation rather than a forecast. The deterministic Tire Pressure page (four-corner radial gauges, soft-low/normal/soft-high threshold bands, warning banner, summary metric cards, pressure history chart, history table) remains the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

alert-tuning-suggestions.label: Alert-rule tuning suggestions
alert-tuning-suggestions.description: Opt-in LLM that reads an existing AlertRule plus the rule's recent 30-day firing history and proposes a typed lower-noise patch (threshold, cooldown, severity, trigger-mode) — for example, raising the battery-low threshold or lengthening the cooldown when the rule has been firing 23 times a week. Surfaces a descriptive replay of the recent firing window (how often the rule would have fired under the proposed thresholds), explicitly NOT a prediction, and never persists the patch — the user reviews the typed draft inside the AlertStudio editor and clicks the canonical Save button to apply. The deterministic AlertStudio editor (manual threshold + cooldown tuning, severity selector, trigger-mode toggle, fired-history table) remains the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

inbox-auto-categorization.label: Inbox auto-categorization
inbox-auto-categorization.description: Opt-in LLM that reads recent notification-log rows for the requested vehicle plus severity filter, buckets them into a closed taxonomy of nine categories (battery, charging, climate, tire, security, connectivity, maintenance, noise, other) using a deterministic substring mapper over the alert rule's signal name, and proposes which category buckets dominate the inbox over the recent window. Surfaces a descriptive count over the chosen window — explicitly NOT a forecast — and never assigns labels to rows; the user reviews the typed proposal inside the inbox panel and clicks Apply categories as filter to copy the proposed rule_id list into the existing URL-backed inbox filter. The deterministic inbox (manual severity / vehicle / rule_id filters, free-text search, day-grouped + threaded views, bulk actions) remains the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

cross-rule-conflict-detection.label: Cross-rule conflict detection
cross-rule-conflict-detection.description: Opt-in LLM that reads the typed AlertRule definitions in the current scope (optionally narrowed by vehicle, signal name, enabled-only, or an explicit rule-id list) and surfaces structural conflicts within a closed taxonomy of two kinds: redundant_duplicate (byte-identical predicate plus overlapping vehicle scope, both enabled) and overlapping_threshold (same signal_name, overlapping vehicle scope, predicate intervals overlap on numeric ops). Each surfaced conflict carries metadata flags for severity_mismatch, cooldown_mismatch, trigger_mode_mismatch, and subsumes — informational only, never a new conflict kind. Descriptive structural overlap analysis only — explicitly NOT a prediction — and never edits, merges, or deletes rules; the user clicks Review rule {id} to navigate the AlertStudio editor and applies any change manually. The deterministic AlertStudio rule list and per-rule validation remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

auto-name-unnamed-locations.label: Auto-name unnamed locations
auto-name-unnamed-locations.description: Opt-in LLM-assisted location-name proposals grounded in the visited-location's visit pattern (current address_name, visit_count, total_duration_s, last_visited). Propose-only: Helix produces a structured proposal via two typed read-only tools (draft_location_name then validate_location_name) and the user explicitly confirms or edits before saving through the existing baseline geofence-create / location-rename path. The deterministic visited-location stat cards, frequency bar charts, and existing list rendered by LocationsPage at /locations remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off. The per-feature redaction policy keeps lat/long, street addresses, and place names tagged; only the vehicle name may be narrated.

geofence-aware-automation-suggestions.label: Geofence-aware automation suggestions
geofence-aware-automation-suggestions.description: Opt-in LLM that proposes a typed Automation graph DTO scoped to one of your existing geofences. Propose-only: Helix proposes a structured automation via two typed read-only tools (draft_automation_graph then validate_automation_graph) and you review the populated form and click Save through the canonical baseline POST /api/v1/automations write path. The geofence catalog (id + name + category — never coordinates) is injected so the LLM picks an existing place_id rather than hallucinating one. The deterministic AutomationBuilder form, trigger / condition / action editors, and Save button at /automations/builder remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

learned-per-vehicle-anomaly-baselines.label: Learned per-vehicle anomaly baselines
learned-per-vehicle-anomaly-baselines.description: Opt-in statistical model that computes per-signal mean, stddev, and p5/p95 from this vehicle's recent signal history (default 14 days, capped at 30) and proposes a learned anomaly envelope, falling back per-signal to the static safe-range envelope when fewer than 30 samples exist in the lookback window. Read-only: the trainer never writes to signal_log, never overwrites the deterministic safe-range table, and the Helix narration walks the user through the learned vs. static comparison via two typed tools (train_anomaly_baseline then query_anomaly_baseline). The deterministic Z-score detector + static safeRanges map at /anomaly-detection remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

range-prediction-model.label: Range-prediction model
range-prediction-model.description: Opt-in statistical model that computes per-bucket (temperature × speed) mean Wh/km from this vehicle's recent drives (default 14 days, capped at 30) and proposes a learned range envelope, falling back per-bucket to the deterministic linear projection when fewer than 5 qualifying drives exist in the lookback window. Read-only: the trainer never writes to drives, never overwrites the heuristic curve, and the Helix narration walks the user through the learned vs. heuristic comparison via two typed tools (train_range_model then query_range_prediction). The deterministic linear projection + heuristic Wh/km curve at /projected-range remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

log-trace-summarization.label: Log and trace summarization
log-trace-summarization.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that summarizes one in-scope window of redacted log events and trace spans into a 3-6 sentence factual paragraph — what level breakdown the window held, which message templates dominated, which trace operations ran (with mean latency), and any structural signals worth investigating — by routing through two read-only tools that quote the same deterministic envelope the operator can already inspect manually. The narrator never invents log lines and never speculates about root cause. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-window tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via operator-authored log messages. The deterministic SSE-backed live log table, level / grep / vehicle filter controls, pause/resume, and copy-to-clipboard / download controls on the Live Logs page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

feedback-queue-triage.label: Feedback queue triage
feedback-queue-triage.description: Opt-in LLM advisor that proposes a status, category, and priority label for one in-scope user feedback row — by quoting the same redacted envelope (id, category, title, body excerpt, page route, app version, status, created_at) that an operator can already inspect manually in the queue — and routes the proposal through a closed-enum validator before the UI surfaces it as a recommendation chip. The advisor NEVER writes to user_feedback; the existing manual triage controls (status dropdown, category badge, priority chip, save button) remain the sole write path. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-row tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via user-authored feedback text. The deterministic feedback queue table, filter / sort / search controls, per-row expansion, and manual triage controls on the Admin Feedback Queue page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

mqtt-sse-inspector-explanations.label: MQTT and SSE inspector explanations
mqtt-sse-inspector-explanations.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that summarizes one in-scope window of the MQTT broker, SSE hub, and background-job state into a 3-6 sentence factual paragraph — whether the broker is connected, how many vehicles are actively streaming, how many are stale, what aggregate signals-per-second the pipeline holds, how many SSE clients are subscribed, and whether the background jobs (signal_log writer, snapshot rollover, alert engine) ran recently — by routing through two read-only tools that quote the same deterministic broker-status envelope the operator can already inspect manually. The narrator never invents a stream state and never speculates about root cause. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-window tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via broker topic strings. Broker hostnames, ports, SSE client identifiers, and VINs are redacted before the message reaches the provider. The deterministic broker-status snapshot panel, per-vehicle stream stats table, throughput chart, and topic-pattern badges on the MQTT Inspector page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

state-machine-debugger-narrator.label: State-machine debugger narrator
state-machine-debugger-narrator.description: Opt-in LLM narrator that summarizes one in-scope vehicle FSM transition trace into a 3-6 sentence factual paragraph — the total transition count, the per-FSM-name breakdown when more than one FSM is present, the dominant from→to edges, the flap count when greater than zero, and any unusual trigger string — by routing through two read-only tools that quote the same deterministic transition envelope the operator can already inspect manually in the transition table. The narrator never invents a transition and never speculates about root cause. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-vehicle or cross-window tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via operator-readable trigger strings or FSM names. VINs, coordinates, place names, IPs, and personal identifiers are redacted before the message reaches the provider. The deterministic transition table, state diagram, FSM health panel, and timeline chart on the State Machine Debugger page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

predictive-maintenance.label: Predictive maintenance
predictive-maintenance.description: Opt-in LLM advisor that narrates one in-scope vehicle's upcoming maintenance risks in a 3-6 sentence factual paragraph — which scheduled items are overdue, which are due soon, the recent service-record context, and whether the current mileage informs the recommendation or if time-based reasoning was used (when no recent odometer reading is available) — by routing through two read-only tools that quote the same deterministic maintenance envelope the operator can already inspect on the Maintenance page. The advisor never invents an item, never proposes a write, and never speculates about root cause beyond the deterministic envelope. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-vehicle tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via user-authored service-record notes. VINs, coordinates, place names, IPs, and personal identifiers are redacted before the message reaches the provider. The deterministic threshold reminders, status badges, summary metric cards, upcoming items list, and Schedule Maintenance write controls on the Maintenance page remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

tco-narration.label: TCO narration
tco-narration.description: Opt-in Helix narrator that explains the deterministic Total-Cost-of-Ownership envelope on the True Cost of Ownership page — the EV charging cost, the equivalent gas cost, the cumulative savings, and the cost-per-kilometre comparison — by routing through one read-only tool that quotes the same numbers the chart shows. The narrator is honest about the four limiting assumptions: operating cost only (no depreciation, resale, insurance, registration, or financing); a flat $50/month maintenance heuristic; equivalent gas cost estimated from charged energy not real-world distance; and gas-price / efficiency / electricity-rate defaults from your editable Settings. When the deterministic envelope reports negative savings the narrator states that fact honestly rather than cheerlead. The deterministic hero stat cards, cumulative-savings area chart, cost-per-km bar chart, monthly EV-vs-gas bar chart, and savings-breakdown summary remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

software-update-changelog-summarizer.label: Software update changelog summarizer
software-update-changelog-summarizer.description: Opt-in Helix narrator that summarizes one in-scope vehicle's firmware update history on the Software Updates page — the current installed version, the install cadence (days between recent versions), and the headline release-note themes for the versions you have actually installed — by routing through two read-only tools that quote the same deterministic update events the timeline shows plus the public Tesla release-note chunks the retrieval layer surfaces. The narrator never invents firmware versions and never claims features your installed build does not have; when no release notes are available for a version it states that fact honestly. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-vehicle tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration via release-note text. The deterministic current-version metric card, install-count metric card, total-update count, the per-version timeline with status chips, and the public release-notes external links remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

pii-redaction-shared-exports.label: PII redaction in shared exports
pii-redaction-shared-exports.description: Opt-in Helix advisor that recommends which PII classes to redact from a shared export on the Exports page — the highly-recommended classes for the chosen export type (drives, charging, trips, analytics, backup, account) plus the optional classes that depend on your consent — by routing through two read-only tools that consult a STATIC catalog of PII classes keyed by export type. The advisor is catalog-based, not a per-row PII scan: Helix never reads the rows of your export and never reports PII it actually saw; it surfaces the catalog's recommendations plus the assumptions inherited from the catalog. Per-request scope binding rejects any cross-export-type tool call to defend against prompt-injection exfiltration. The deterministic export-jobs list, bulk-delete toolbar, and download links remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

nl-sql-playground.label: Natural-language SQL playground
nl-sql-playground.description: Opt-in Helix translator on the SQL Playground page (/power/sql) that converts a natural-language question into a typed read-only SQL DRAFT (a single SELECT or WITH statement against the curated install-wide schema catalog of drives, charging_sessions, vehicles, alerts, and signal_log_view) by routing through two propose-only tools (draft_readonly_sql + validate_readonly_sql). The translator NEVER executes SQL — there is no apply or execute tool; the deny-by-default keyword scan refuses INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, CREATE, TRUNCATE, GRANT, REVOKE, VACUUM, COPY, CALL, DO, MERGE, and EXECUTE; the per-request scope binding refuses any table reference outside the curated catalog. The user reviews the typed proposal in the AI side panel, clicks Apply to editor to copy the draft into the manual SQL editor, and clicks the canonical Run button to execute. The deterministic manual SQL editor and curated catalog viewer remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

nl-grafana-panel.label: Natural-language Grafana panel
nl-grafana-panel.description: Opt-in Helix translator on the Grafana Panel Builder page (/power/grafana) that converts a natural-language data question into a typed Grafana panel JSON DRAFT (a single panel envelope — title, type, datasource, targets, grid_pos — against the curated install-wide panel-builder catalog of 8 panel types, 2 datasource types, and the same 5 tables nl-sql-playground exposes) by routing through two propose-only tools (draft_grafana_panel + validate_grafana_panel). The translator NEVER pushes the panel to Grafana — there is no apply or push tool; the per-request scope binding refuses any panel type, datasource type, or table outside the curated catalog; the postgres rawSql contract refuses anything other than a SELECT/WITH single statement. The user reviews the typed proposal in the AI side panel, clicks Apply to editor to copy the draft into the manual JSON editor, and clicks the canonical Copy to clipboard button to paste it into their existing Grafana dashboard. The deterministic manual JSON editor and curated panel-builder catalog viewer remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

nl-dashboard-composer.label: Natural-language dashboard composer
nl-dashboard-composer.description: Opt-in Helix translator on the Dashboard Composer page (/power/dashboards) that converts a natural-language dashboard request into a typed dashboard JSON DRAFT (a single dashboard envelope — title + ordered list of panel slots picking panels by name from the curated install-wide catalog and placing each on the Grafana 24-column grid) by routing through two propose-only tools (draft_dashboard_layout + validate_dashboard_layout). The translator NEVER pushes the dashboard to Grafana — there is no apply or push tool; the per-request scope binding refuses any panel_name outside the curated catalog; the layout contract refuses overlapping bounding boxes, more than 12 slots, or the same panel_name twice. The user reviews the typed proposal in the AI side panel, clicks Apply to editor to copy the draft into the manual JSON dashboard composer, and clicks the canonical Copy to clipboard button to paste it into their existing Grafana dashboard. The deterministic manual JSON composer and curated panel catalog viewer remain the canonical baseline when Helix is off.

settingsBackup.subtitle: Export your TeslaSync configuration as a JSON file you can stash in a backup folder or git repo, and import it on a fresh install.

export.title: Export settings
export.help: Includes general settings, alert rules, geofences, and your quiet-hours windows. Tesla credentials and notification-channel secrets are NEVER exported.

import.title: Import settings
import.help: Drop or pick a previously exported bundle. Existing items with the same name are updated; nothing is deleted.
import.dropPrompt: Drag a JSON bundle here, or

settingsReset.title: Reset to defaults
settingsReset.subtitle: Restore an individual section to its default state. Each reset is destructive and cannot be undone — export your settings first if you want a backup.
settingsReset.deniedSubtitle: These sections live outside this server’s preference store. The Settings page can’t reset them, but the linked instructions tell you where to go.

general.title: General preferences
general.desc: Units, language, currency, timezone, and energy/gas pricing defaults.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.desc: Theme, density, chart palette, and notification badge / flash preferences.

alertRules.title: Alert rules
alertRules.desc: Delete every alert rule you have authored. Cannot be undone.

geofences.title: Geofences
geofences.desc: Delete every geofence and its electricity-rate overrides. Vehicle home assignments will be cleared.

notificationChannels.title: Notification channels
notificationChannels.desc: Delete every webhook, Discord, Slack, email, and push channel along with their delivery history.

dashboardLayout.title: Dashboard layouts
dashboardLayout.desc: Delete every saved dashboard layout preset.

automations.title: Automations
automations.desc: Delete every automation, including its triggers, conditions, actions, variables, and run history.

quietHours.title: Quiet hours
quietHours.desc: Delete every quiet-hours window for your account.

tariffs.title: Charge cost tariffs
tariffs.reason: Tariffs are stored per-vehicle. Reset the assignment from the Vehicle Settings page on the vehicle detail screen.

soundPrefs.title: Notification sound preferences
soundPrefs.reason: Notification sound preferences are stored in your browser. Clear them via your browser’s site-data controls.

dangerZone.title: Danger zone
dangerZone.subtitle: Wipe every user-discoverable preference at once. Alert rules, geofences, channels, automations, dashboard layouts, and your typed preference rows are all deleted in a single transaction.
dangerZone.help: You will be asked to type RESET to confirm.

confirm.allMessage: Every alert rule, geofence, channel, automation, dashboard layout preset, and preference row will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.

webhookChannels.title: Webhook channels
webhookChannels.subtitle: Forward TeslaSync notifications to Discord, Slack, n8n, Home Assistant, or any HTTP receiver. Each channel can be HMAC-signed so receivers can verify authenticity.

empty.title: No webhooks yet
empty.message: Add a webhook to forward TeslaSync events to your favourite chat or automation tool.

form.name: Name
form.urlInvalid: URL must start with http:// or https://.
form.urlHelp: Compatible with Discord, Slack, n8n, Home Assistant, and any HTTP receiver.
form.secretHelp: When set, every request includes X-TeslaSync-Signature: sha256=<hmac> so the receiver can verify authenticity.

signature.label: Signature preview
signature.empty: Add a signing secret to preview the X-TeslaSync-Signature header.
signature.help: Send this header value with every webhook so receivers can verify authenticity.

delete.title: Delete webhook?
delete.message: This will permanently remove the webhook. TeslaSync will stop sending notifications to it immediately.

docs.title: Available payload variables
docs.intro: Webhook receivers get a JSON envelope with these fields:

rateLimitStatus.title: Rate-limit budgets
rateLimitStatus.subtitle: Live view of every server-side throttle that affects this TeslaSync deployment. Bars climb as the window fills; colour switches from green to amber at 50% and to red at 80%.
rateLimitStatus.error: Could not load rate-limit status. Check API logs and try again.
rateLimitStatus.empty: No rate-limited resources are currently observed. Counters appear here once the API has handled at least one request.

queueStatus.title: Background workers
queueStatus.subtitle: Live view of the notification, export, and automation worker queues. Heartbeat colour switches from green to amber after 60 seconds and to red after 5 minutes of silence; "down" means the worker has never reported in.
queueStatus.error: Could not load worker status. Check API logs and try again.
queueStatus.empty: No workers are currently registered. The notification, export, and automation processes report here once they start.

drawer.title: Recent jobs
drawer.error: Could not load recent jobs. Check API logs and try again.
drawer.empty: No recent jobs to show. New jobs will appear here as the worker processes them.

settingsSessions.title: Active sessions
settingsSessions.subtitle: Devices currently signed in to TeslaSync. Revoking a session signs that browser out on its next request — your upstream identity provider's session is unaffected.

openMode.title: Active sessions
openMode.message: Active session tracking requires forward-auth mode. Configure your reverse proxy to inject X-Forwarded-User then reload.

settingsSessions.empty: No active sessions for this account.

confirm.revokeMessage: {{device}} will be signed out on its next request. Your other devices will stay signed in.
confirm.allOthersMessage: Every browser other than this one will be signed out on its next request. You can sign back in immediately.

vehicleSettings.title: Per-vehicle settings
vehicleSettings.subtitle: Override individual settings for this vehicle. Resets fall back to your account-wide values.

nickname.label: Nickname
nickname.help: Friendly name shown in the vehicle list and page title.

mute_until.label: Mute alerts until
mute_until.help: Suppresses alerts for this vehicle until the chosen date and time. Clear to receive alerts immediately.

charge_cost_tariff_id.label: Charge cost tariff
charge_cost_tariff_id.help: Tariff identifier used when calculating per-session charge costs for this vehicle.

units_distance.label: Distance unit
units_distance.help: Override the distance unit (mi or km) for this vehicle's panels.

units_temperature.label: Temperature unit
units_temperature.help: Override the temperature unit (°C or °F) for this vehicle's panels.

units_energy.label: Energy unit
units_energy.help: Override the energy display unit (kWh) for this vehicle's panels.

validation.invalid: Value is not valid for this setting.
validation.invalidDate: Enter a valid date and time.

openMode.message: The RBAC matrix is meaningful only when an upstream proxy (Authentik, Authelia, oauth2-proxy, Keycloak, etc.) injects an authenticated subject header. Configure FORWARD_AUTH_HEADER and TESLASYNC_RBAC_GROUPS_HEADER on the API service then reload.

effective.tooltip: Permissions effective for your current roles

banner.title: Impersonating {{target}}
banner.body: You are viewing TeslaSync as another subject. End impersonation to restore your session.

confirm.title: Start impersonation session?
confirm.message: You will see TeslaSync as {{subject}} for up to 15 minutes. The action is logged to the audit log. End the session from the banner when you are done.

users.title: Subjects
users.subtitle: Active subjects you can impersonate for support. Sessions are limited to 15 minutes and recorded in the audit log.
users.openMode: Impersonation requires forward-auth mode. This install is in open mode, so per-user identity is not available.
users.emptyMessage: No other subjects have an active session right now. Sign someone else in to enable impersonation.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.subtitle: Manage local browsing history surfaces. These settings only affect this browser.

recentPages.empty: Pages you visit will appear here for quick access.
recentPages.clearBody: Wipe the list of pages used by the dashboard widget and the Recent section in the command palette.
recentPages.clearConfirmBody: This will wipe the list immediately. The dashboard widget and palette Recent section will be empty until you visit new pages.

slo.title: Uptime & SLO
slo.caveat: Per-window historical uptime requires the heartbeat history backend (planned). This figure reflects the current snapshot.
slo.empty: No uptime data for this window yet.

aiRedaction.title: Plan PII redactions before sharing
aiRedaction.description: Ask Helix to recommend which PII classes to redact from a shared export. The recommendation is catalog-based — Helix never reads the rows of your export; it consults a deterministic per-export-type PII catalog and surfaces the highly-recommended redactions plus the optional ones that depend on your consent. Apply the recommendation by toggling the matching options in your export request.
aiRedaction.noTypeHint: Pick an export type to enable Helix.

aiAutoName.title: Suggest a name for this location
aiAutoName.description: Propose a concise, human-readable name for this visited location based on its visit pattern. Review only — Helix never saves the name; you confirm and save via the existing baseline form.

errors.invalidCode: Code did not match. Try the next one.

safetySettings.pageSubtitle: Notification quiet hours, alert digest mode, critical-flash signalling, tab-badge signalling, and the API kill-switch. Use the links below each row to change a value.

listing.title: Your safety-related settings
listing.subtitle: Each row shows the current value on this install and links to the canonical Settings page where you can change it.
listing.changeHint: To change a value, open the main Settings page. This page is read-only and never changes a setting on its own.

quietHoursEnabled.title: Quiet hours
quietHoursEnabled.description: When ON, TeslaSync defers non-critical notifications during the configured quiet-hours window. Critical alerts are always delivered.

quietHoursStart.title: Quiet-hours window start
quietHoursStart.description: Window start in HH:MM (24-hour) local time. Effective only when quiet hours are ON.

quietHoursEnd.title: Quiet-hours window end
quietHoursEnd.description: Window end in HH:MM (24-hour) local time. Effective only when quiet hours are ON.

alertDigestMode.title: Alert digest mode
alertDigestMode.description: How alerts are batched. Instant delivers each alert as it fires; Hourly batches into one digest per hour; Daily batches into one digest per day.

criticalFlashEnabled.title: Critical-alert tab flash
criticalFlashEnabled.description: When ON, TeslaSync briefly flashes the browser tab title when a critical alert arrives while the tab is in the background. Honours the OS-level reduce-motion preference.

tabBadgeEnabled.title: Unread tab badge
tabBadgeEnabled.description: When ON, TeslaSync prefixes the browser tab title with (N) and paints a coloured dot on the favicon for unread notifications.

apiSuspended.title: API kill-switch
apiSuspended.description: Operational kill-switch. When ON, TeslaSync stops issuing requests to the Tesla Fleet API; existing telemetry streams continue. Used during outage triage so the install does not pile up rate-limited retries.

aiExplainer.title: Explain my safety settings
aiExplainer.description: Ask Helix to explain the safety-related TeslaSync settings on this page in plain English. Helix only reads the typed envelope of canonical setting values (booleans, enum strings, HH:MM times) — it never reads notification titles, vehicle names, or any other PII, and it never proposes or changes a setting. Use the controls below to update a value yourself; Helix only narrates.

voiceMode.title: Voice mode
voiceMode.description: Speak to Helix and hear the reply out loud. Voice input and playback both stay on this device — only the transcribed text is sent to the assistant, never the raw audio.
voiceMode.idleHint: Tap the mic and ask Helix anything about your Tesla.
voiceMode.unsupportedHint: Voice input is not available in this browser. You can still type your question into the chatbot below.
voiceMode.emptyHint: Tap the mic and dictate a question first.

errors.unsupported: Your browser does not support voice input. Try Chrome, Edge, or Safari.

watchFaceNL.title: Ask Helix about your watch face
watchFaceNL.description: Ask Helix a glance-style natural-language question about your vehicle right now — battery, range, charging, locks, climate, recent alerts. Helix only reads a typed snapshot of canonical state values; it never claims to have changed a setting or sent a vehicle command. To lock, unlock, start climate, or send another command use the watch-face tap icons or the phone app.
watchFaceNL.placeholder: e.g. how is my battery? Is the car locked? Leave empty for a summary.
